rows.name: Local Poke Bowl
rows.description: Poke bowl vendor named at the Haleiwa Farmers Market
rows.notes: Hawaii News Now (March 7, 2025) named Local Poke Bowl among vendors at the Thursday 2–6 PM Haleiwa Farmers Market, hosted by FarmLovers. A Haleiwa Town guide later said the FarmLovers Haleiwa market was temporarily closed, and I found no current vendor or organizer page confirming this vendor. Sources disagree on the market's place and day: HNN says the Historic Haleiwa Gym property, Thursdays; the guide and other pages say Liliuokalani Church grounds. The Honolulu Night Market entry from the first pass was dropped because I could not confirm it. Instagram handle comes from a 2022 Star-Advertiser feature, which also listed Waialua, Waimea and Pearlridge markets that are not confirmed as current. Address omitted because only listing sites showed one.

rows.notes: Own site says it is a pop-up truck across Oʻahu, typically Saturday and Sunday pop-ups; locations are posted on Instagram @mealsontheflyhi, or call or text 808-223-9840. Site lists burritos at $12–$20 and meal prep at $15 or $18 per meal, ordered by Wednesday for Saturday or Sunday pickup. Email is mealsontheflyhi@gmail.com. Also on the Koʻolau Night Market list for June 12, 2026. The business writes its name 'Meals on the Fly'; the organizer's spelling is kept in the name field. Plenty of Aloha's markets page also names 'Meals on the Fly' in a vendor list, but which market it belongs to is unclear, so it is not added.

rows.notes: Own market page shows the North Shore Country Market, Wednesdays 12–5 at Queen Liliʻuokalani Church, 66-090 Kamehameha Hwy, Haleʻiwa (page for Feb 18, 2026). Instagram bio gives Saturdays 8–12 at Kaka'ako Farmer's Market; the bio has no posting date. The Mele Kalikimaka booth (#25, 2025) is from the first pass; a 2026 show is not confirmed. Own Markets + Stockists page also lists retail stockists: The Cove Collection North Shore (59-712 B Kamehameha Hwy, Haleiwa), The Cove Collection Reef Waikīkī, and Nā Mea Hawaiʻi (Ala Moana). Hive locations are not given as an address; own page says apiaries from Waialua to Hauʻula.
